scenario: AITA for giving my girlfriend pointers on how to cook better? | So my girlfriend is pissed at me and has a cooking "strike" because, and I quote,"if you are so much better than me at cooking you can do it yourself". We moved in together 6 months ago (been together for 2 before it) and we came to an agreement that she will do the cooking since she comes 2h earlier from work and I was all on board for having a hot meal ready when I come home. The thing is she is not exactly good at it. She isnt terrible, everything she makes is edible but is far off from the standard I was used to. So, I started to give her pointers. After all she cant get better if she doesnt know that something is off. I would tell her whenever she used too little salt or too much spice, if something was a little burnt or undercooked, told her when I knew how to make the dish better next time etc. I would always eat all of it and say thank you so it was not like I was being rude about it. The thing is that she "snapped" when my mother came to visit and I casually said that she could give my girlfriend some cooking advice. My girlfriend nodded and smiled and generally seemed fine in the moment but as soon as the doors closed behind my mother my girlfriend went ballistic, accused me of humiliating her and her cooking in front of my family and stormed off. Since then I apologised saying that I am sorry for giving her constructive criticism in front of my mom but it didnt calm her much and she still refuses to make anything food-related at home for me. I think she is overreacting, I never complained about her cooking or throw it out. I was just being helpful. I miss her cooking, not gonna lie, so I might as well ask here if I stepped over the line somewhere. AITA or is my girlfriend crazy?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I'm being AITA (a jerk) or if my girlfriend is overreacting. Let me start by understanding the situation. We've been together for 2 years, and we moved in together 6 months ago. We agreed that she would handle cooking because she gets home earlier from work, and I like having a hot meal ready when I come home. That makes sense because I don't want to cook every day, and she's the one who's usually home earlier. But here's the thing: she's not the best cook. Her food is edible, but it's far from what I was used to before we moved in together. I mean, it's not terrible, but it's definitely not up to my standards. So, I started giving her pointers. I thought, hey, she can get better if she knows what's off. I told her when she used too little salt or too much spice, or if something was a bit burned or undercooked. I even told her how to make the dish better next time. I always ate everything and said thank you, so I wasn't being rude about it. But then, my mom came over, and I casually mentioned that she could give my girlfriend some cooking advice. My girlfriend nodded and smiled, seemed fine at the moment. But as soon as the door closed behind my mom, she went ballistic. She accused me of humiliating her and her cooking in front of my family and stormed off. Since then, I've apologized, saying I'm sorry for giving her constructive criticism in front of my mom, but it didn't calm her much. She still refuses to make anything food-related at home for me. I think she's overreacting. I never complained about her cooking or threw it out. I was just being helpful. I miss her cooking, not going to lie, so I might as well ask her if I stepped over the lines somewhere. Is it AITA or is my girlfriend crazy? Hmm, so I need to figure out whether I'm being a jerk or if my girlfriend is overreacting. Let's break it down. First, I started giving her pointers on her cooking. I thought it was helpful, but maybe she felt criticized. Even though I was polite about it, she might have felt that I was implying her cooking wasn't good enough. That could be hurtful, especially if she's trying her best. Then, when my mom came over, I mentioned that she could give my girlfriend some cooking advice. That might have been the tipping point. My girlfriend might have felt that I was not only criticizing her but also involving my mom to do the same, which could make her feel even more humiliated. She snapped and accused me of humiliating her in front of my family. That's a strong reaction, but it's possible that she felt that way. Maybe she felt that I was undermining her in front of someone else, which could make her feel insecure or inadequate. I apologized for giving her constructive criticism in front of my mom, but she's still upset. She's refusing to cook for me, which is a significant issue because it affects our daily routine. So, is it AITA or is she overreacting? I think there's a bit of both. On one hand, I was trying to help her improve her cooking, which is a good intention. On the other hand, the way I delivered the criticism might have come off as more critical than helpful, especially in front of my mom. Maybe I should have handled the situation differently. Instead of giving her pointers in front of my mom, I could have talked to her privately about it. That way, she wouldn't feel humiliated in front of someone else. Also, involving my mom in giving her advice might have made her feel like I was teaming up against her, which could have made her more defensive. It's important to approach such sensitive topics with care and sensitivity, especially when it comes to relationships. In the future, I should consider how she feels about receiving criticism, especially in front of others. Maybe I can find a better way to offer help without making her feel criticized or humiliated. Overall, I think I stepped over the line a bit by giving her constructive criticism in front of my mom, which might have made her feel insecure. However, she might also be overreacting by taking it so personally and refusing to cook for me. It's a delicate balance, and communication is key in resolving such issues.
